source: ADR-0050, 2026-09-25. Numbers are configuration under ADR-0031, not constants.
closed_after_polled_runs_note: A posting has closed when absent from its board on this many consecutive runs that polled it. Twelve, about six days at two runs a day, the operator's decision of 2026-10-03: twelve Greenhouse postings left their boards and returned after 23 to 130 hours, median 59 (measured 2026-09-30 over the run logs), so the starting value of four, about 48 hours, would have closed more than half of them while open. A closed row is hidden from his To review view.
retire_after_days_note: Classified rows are stored and leave Jobs, rejection copies are deleted, and closed rows are retired this many days after their clock starts. The operator's figure, carried from ADR-0046.
unreviewed_after_days_note: ADR-0055's clock: a row nobody classified leaves Jobs this many days after it was first seen, stored with the reason unreviewed-aged-out first. The chat's starting value, approved by the operator 2026-09-28: double the fifteen-day retention.
clearing_dry_run_valid_hours_note: ADR-0055's tool removes nothing unless a dry run of the same table and threshold ran on this branch within this many hours. The implementing seat's value, approved by the operator 2026-09-30: long enough to read the dry run's report and decide the next day.
run_log_window_note: How many recent run logs the closure test reads: thirty days at two runs a day.
reason_choices_note: ADR-0062: the choices of each rejection table's reason field, Choice reason and Pipeline reason, as they stand in the operator's base. The sweep writes his Reason from Jobs into a new copy's reason field only when it is one of these, so a value the field does not offer cannot fail a whole batch; any other value is kept in the store record and named in the run log. A choice he adds in Airtable is added here too, or it is kept in the store only.
description_fields_shown_note: Brief 13: whether the projection sends the description's values to Jobs, Years asked, Required in, On site and No description, which the pipeline owns. Off until the operator has made the four fields in Jobs and Jobs test, since a read or write naming a field the table lacks fails the call, and until the month has room for the one re-send of every row they cost, about 16 calls at 150 rows: from 2026-11-01, the date Brief 13 sets, or sooner if his count shows room. Turned on by a commit, never by a date in code. On since 2026-11-01, the date Brief 13 set.
sources_held_from_display_note: ADR-0063: sources fetched, judged at first sight and stored, but not sent to Jobs while the month's allowance cannot carry their rows, the operator's rule of 2026-10-18: 'if quota is an issue then just do not do api call and only build.' Held only when the projection of the month says so; released by a commit when it has room, at the latest when the next month resets. Empty on 2026-10-18: Hacker News' rows, about one a day read fresh, cost a fraction of a call each, and October holds without them held (the seat's report on Brief 16).
monthly_call_ceiling_note: ADR-0062: the pipeline refuses any Airtable call that would take its own month's count to this figure. Airtable's limit is the workspace's 1,000, which the chats' connector calls also spend and the pipeline cannot see, so the hundred between is theirs. Reaching it stops the projection and the sweep, each run exiting 2, and leaves the fetch and its stores untouched; the display catches up when the month resets. The operator's decision of 2026-10-16: '900 for now'. What he watches is the workspace's Usage count.
budget_warning_note: Say so loudly when the month's Airtable calls pass this share of the allowance before this day of the month. ADR-0050's guard; ADR-0004 says why the warning must be ours.
